title: Living & Non-Living Things
description: Grade 2 Science: living and non-living things. What makes something alive, what living things need, and once-living things — with sorting games and a home hunt.

topics.title: What Is Living?
topics.concept:
Living things are alive. We can tell because they do special things:

  • 🌱 They grow — they get bigger.
  • 🍎 They need food and water.
  • 🌬️ They breathe air.
  • 🐾 They can move on their own.
  • 🐣 They make young ones (babies or seeds).

People, animals and plants are all living things.

recap: Living things grow, eat, breathe, move and make young ones.
People, animals and plants are living.
Doing these special things shows something is alive.

wonder.text: A dog runs and eats. A rock just sits still. What makes the dog alive and the rock not?

qa.q: Plants can't run, so how are they living?
qa.a: Plants do not run, but they still grow, drink water, breathe and make seeds. Moving is only one sign of life — plants do all the others!
Yes! A seed is resting, but it is alive. Give it water and warmth and it will wake up and grow into a plant.

topics.title: Non-Living Things
topics.concept:
Non-living things are not alive. They do not grow, eat, breathe or move on their own.

  • 🪨 A rock
  • 🪑 A chair
  • ⚽ A ball
  • 🚗 A toy car
  • 🥄 A spoon

A toy car can roll only when YOU push it. It cannot move by itself, so it is non-living.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 330 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="330" height="150" fill="#f3f4f7"/><text x="55" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🪨</text><text x="55" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Rock</text><text x="165" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🪑</text><text x="165" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Chair</text><text x="275" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">⚽</text><text x="275" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Ball</text><text x="165" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">Non-living things</text></svg>
recap: Non-living things do not grow, eat, breathe or move on their own.
Rocks, chairs, balls and toys are non-living.
A toy car moves only when we push it.

wonder.text: Your toy car has wheels, but it cannot drive away by itself. Why not?

qa.q: A river moves — is it living?
qa.a: Good question! A river moves, but it does not eat, grow or breathe. The water is pushed downhill by gravity. So a river is non-living.

qa.q: Why isn't a toy puppy alive?
qa.a: A toy puppy may look cute, but it cannot eat, grow or breathe on its own. Only a real puppy does those living things.

topics.title: Living or Non-Living?
topics.concept:
To decide, ask these questions about the thing:

  • Does it grow on its own? 🌱
  • Does it need food and water? 🍎
  • Does it breathe? 🌬️
  • Can it move by itself? 🐾

If the answer is yes, it is living. If the answer is no, it is non-living.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="320" height="150" fill="#fff"/><rect x="10" y="14" width="146" height="120" rx="12" fill="#d8f5e3"/><text x="50" y="74" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🐕</text><text x="106" y="74" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🌳</text><text x="83" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Living</text><rect x="164" y="14" width="146" height="120" rx="12" fill="#e6e8ee"/><text x="204" y="74" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🪨</text><text x="260" y="74" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🥄</text><text x="237" y="116" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Non-living</text></svg>
recap: Ask: does it grow, eat, breathe and move on its own?
The Sun and clouds are non-living.

wonder.text: How can you be sure if something is living or non-living? What would you check?

qa.q: Is the Sun living because it gives light?
qa.a: No. The Sun is very important, but it does not grow, eat or breathe. It is a giant ball of hot gas — non-living.
Clouds move and change shape, but they do not eat, grow or breathe. They are made of tiny water drops — so they are non-living.

topics.title: What Living Things Need
topics.concept:
Every living thing — people, animals and plants — needs:

  • 🍎 Food — for energy to grow.
  • 💧 Water — to drink.
  • 🌬️ Air — to breathe.
  • 🏠 A place to live — space and shelter.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 360 150" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="360" height="150" fill="#eefff2"/><text x="45" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🍎</text><text x="45" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Food</text><text x="135" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">💧</text><text x="135" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Water</text><text x="225" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🌬️</text><text x="225" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Air</text><text x="315" y="64" font-size="34" text-anchor="middle">🏠</text><text x="315" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="700" fill="#23314f" text-anchor="middle">Home</text><text x="180" y="138" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#555" text-anchor="middle">What living things need</text></svg>
recap: All living things need food, water, air and space.
Plants make their own food using sunlight.
Water is needed by every living thing.

wonder.text: You, a sparrow and a mango tree all need the same few things to live. Can you guess them?

qa.q: Do plants eat food like we do?
qa.a: Plants make their own food in their leaves using sunlight. We have to eat food, but plants are clever cooks who make theirs!

qa.q: What happens if a living thing has no water?
qa.a: Without water, living things become weak and unwell, and they cannot survive for long. That is why water is so precious.

topics.title: Once-Living Things
topics.concept:
Some non-living things were once part of a living thing! They came from plants or animals.

  • 🪑 Wood comes from trees (which were living).
  • 📄 Paper is made from wood.
  • 🧶 Wool comes from sheep.
  • 🍯 Honey comes from bees.

So a wooden chair is non-living now, but the tree it came from was once alive.

recap: Some non-living things were once part of living things.
Wood and paper come from trees; wool from sheep; honey from bees.
Saving paper helps save living trees.

wonder.text: Your wooden chair is non-living now. But was it always non-living?

qa.a: Yes! Cotton grows on the cotton plant. People pick it and turn it into thread and cloth. So your cotton shirt came from a living plant.

qa.q: Why should we not waste paper?
qa.a: Paper is made from trees. Wasting paper means cutting more trees. Using paper carefully helps save living trees!

questions.q: Which one is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A tree grows, drinks water and makes seeds, so it is living.
Living things grow, eat, breathe and move on their own.
A spoon does not grow, eat or breathe — it is non-living.
All living things need food, water, air and a place to live.

questions.q: Which was once part of a living thing?
questions.explanation: Wood comes from trees, which were living.

questions.q: A toy car is non-living because…
options: It cannot move on its own
questions.explanation: A toy car moves only when we push it — it cannot move by itself.

questions.q: Why is the Sun a non-living thing?
options: It does not grow, eat or breathe
questions.explanation: The Sun gives light but does not grow, eat or breathe, so it is non-living.

questions.q: A river moves, but it is non-living because…
options: It does not eat, grow or breathe
questions.explanation: The water is just pushed downhill; a river does not eat, grow or breathe.

questions.q: Which list has only LIVING things?
questions.explanation: Dog, tree and fish all grow, eat and breathe.

questions.q: Wool comes from a sheep, so wool is…
options: A non-living thing that was once part of a living animal
Made in a factory from sand
questions.explanation: Wool is non-living now, but it came from a living sheep.

questions.q: Which is the BEST way to tell if something is living?
options: Check if it grows, eats, breathes and moves on its own
questions.explanation: Living things grow, eat, breathe and move on their own — that is how we tell.
